name: Long-Term Residence Permit for the Purpose of Family Reunification

requirements.blocker_text: Sponsor must hold: a valid long-term or permanent residence permit and have resided in Czechia over 15 months (both spouses aged 20+); OR a valid Employee Card with 6+ months of Czech residence; OR a Blue Card, intra-company transfer card, or investment residence permit; OR a scientific-research permit (or pending application). These sponsor-status conditions do not apply for adoptees, custody children, elderly parents, or asylum-related family applications.

Eligible relatives: spouse or registered partner (including same-sex partnerships); minor children or stepchildren; adult children who are financially dependent or medically incapable of self-care; adopted minors or children in custody; minors whose legal guardian is the sponsor; and single/divorced/widowed parents aged 65+, or parents of any age medically unable to care for themselves.

evidence_required.document: Marriage, birth, or custody documentation proving the relationship
Sponsor's proof of qualifying residence status
Application fee CZK2,500 (CZK1,000 for minors under 15)

outcome.duration_length: matches sponsor's permit duration (minimum 1 year); 2 years initially (extendable to 5) if sponsor holds permanent residence

sources.title: ipc.gov.cz -- Long-Term Residence Permit for the Purpose of Family Reunification: eligible relatives, sponsor-status conditions, asylum-family exceptions, permit duration, free labour-market access

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Czechia's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1. work_rights set to 'full': the source explicitly states holders gain 'free access to the labour market.' After 3 years of residence, holders may apply for an alternative residence purpose (pr_after_months set to 36 reflecting this, though this is a switch to a different status rather than automatic permanent residence -- the source does not describe it as automatic conversion). Additional pathways open at age 18 or upon dissolution of the sponsoring marriage. A distinct, more permissive family-reunification track exists for recognised refugees/asylum beneficiaries (spouses if married before entry, minor children, dependent adult children under 26 in continuing education, parents of minor asylum recipients within 3 months of the grant) -- referenced here rather than modelled as a fully separate file, and covered further in cz_international_protection's notes.
